item.title: Omizutori: The Fire and Water Rites of Todaiji — Guide
item.description: Omizutori is the popular name for Shuni-e, a series of sacred Buddhist rites held at Todaiji’s Nigatsudo hall over the first two weeks of March, and one of Japan’s oldest ceremonies — performed every year without interruption since 752, over 1,270 years. Its most spectacular moment is the Otaimatsu each evening, when monks race along the hall’s wooden veranda swinging enormous flaming pine torches, showering embers over the crowd gathered below (sparks are said to bring good luck and blessing).
